article_title: Audacity 4.0 Ships With a Qt Rewrite, New Clip-Editing Model, and .aup4 Project Format
summary: Duplicate coverage: this submission covers the exact same Audacity 4.0 Qt-rewrite release already published hours earlier as 2026-09/03-audacity-40-rebuilds-the-open-source-audio-editor-on-qt-with-a-new-clip-editing-model.md (PR #2354), with no new angle or substantive update; the submission's Overview lead also contains a specific (prior-release/beta date history) unsupported by any of its six cited sources.

findings.details: This submission covers the same Audacity 4.0 release (Qt interface rewrite, new clip-editing model, Workspaces, .aup4 format, dropped Audacity 3 features) as the article published earlier the same day at src/content/articles/2026-09/03-audacity-40-rebuilds-the-open-source-audio-editor-on-qt-with-a-new-clip-editing-model.md (from PR #2354, merged as commit 9d43a6572). Both draw on overlapping primary sources (GitHub release notes, OMG! Ubuntu June beta and September release coverage). This submission adds citations to audacityteam.org/audacity-4, audacityteam.org homepage, and a short LWN.net item, but these supply only incidental color (download-count stat, accent-color theming detail, a one-paragraph technical-press mention) rather than a new angle, follow-up development, or contradicting information. No Analysis section or comparable added value is present.

The Overview paragraph states the 4.0.0 release followed 'the Audacity 3.7.9 patch released September 1 and a beta cycle that included a 4.0.0 Beta 4 pre-release on August 28.' None of the six cited source snapshots (GitHub release tag page, audacityteam.org/audacity-4, audacityteam.org homepage, both OMG! Ubuntu articles, LWN.net) mention a 3.7.9 patch, a 'Beta 4' pre-release, or the August 28/September 1 dates. This appears to be a fabricated or unverifiable specific placed in the article's lead.

content_preview.title: Audacity 4.0 Ships With a Qt Rewrite, New Clip-Editing Model, and .aup4 Project Format
content_preview.summary: Audacity 4.0 replaces the open-source audio editor's wxWidgets interface with Qt, adds a new clip-editing model, Workspaces, and a .aup4 project format, while dropping several Audacity 3 features.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

Audacity, the open-source multi-track audio editor that the project's [official site](https://www.audacityteam.org/) credits with "100M+ downloads since 2000," released version 4.0.0 on September 3, 2026. The [GitHub release notes](https://github.com/audacity/audacity/releases/tag/Audacity-4.0.0) describe the update as one that "rebuilds the application interface on Qt and introduces many new quality-of-life improvements, including a new clip-editing model." The release is listed as...

editor_notes.content_quality: Well-written and structurally sound — matches the established Overview / What We Know / What We Don't Know format, neutral tone, no AI self-reference. The individual verbatim quotes that ARE sourced are accurately attributed (verified against snapshots below). The defect is not writing quality but originality and one unsourced lead detail.
editor_notes.source_verification: All 6 source snapshots read from sources/2026-09/audacity-40-ships-with-a-qt-rewrite-new-clip-editing-model-and-aup4-project-format/ and sha256-verified against manifest.json (all match). source-0 (github.com/audacity/audacity/releases/tag/Audacity-4.0.0): confirms 'rebuilds the application interface on Qt and introduces many new quality-of-life improvements, including a new clip-editing model', 'The interface has been rebuilt on ... native high-DPI rendering', 'Groups remain together when moved, copied, pasted or duplicated', Time Tracks/Macro Manager-and-scripting-pipe omissions, 'working on adding them in future releases', VST3/Nyquist/LV2/Audio Units plugin list, and the Sep 3 2026 10:19 UTC release timestamp. Does NOT confirm the '3.7.9 patch released September 1' / '4.0.0 Beta 4 pre-release on August 28' claim in the Overview — see findings. source-1 (audacityteam.org/audacity-4): confirms 'Built on Qt ... runs natively on macOS, Windows and Linux', 'Open-standard LV2 plugins load right alongside VST3 and Audio Units, with no wrappers required', 'Each workspace changes the tools in your toolbar ... swaps the ruler between seconds and bars and beats', 'Choose an accent color and apply it throughout your app', 'Switch between light and dark themes, each with a high-contrast variant'. source-2 (audacityteam.org homepage): confirms '100M+ downloads since 2000'. source-3 (OMG! Ubuntu, Sept release): confirms 'more than a superficial ... facelift', 'Easier clip selection', 'Clips grouping', 'Toolbars and panels can be moved, popped-out or closed', the .aup4/preview-thumbnails and one-way-conversion claims, verbatim. source-4 (OMG! Ubuntu, June beta): confirms 'The audio editor's interface, built on wxWidgets since the project began, now runs in Qt.' source-5 (LWN.net): confirms 'a rewritten interface using Qt' and 'not fully feature-compatible with the Audacity 3.x series'. One claim (3.7.9 patch / Beta 4 dates in the Overview) is NOT supported by any of the 6 snapshots — flagged as a finding above.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Every direct quote checked appears verbatim in its cited snapshot. One subordinate specific in the Overview lead (prior patch/beta release history and dates) has no support in any cited source and could not be verified — see findings.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and professional throughout; no editorializing or sensationalism.
editor_notes.originality: REJECT-triggering. This is the second independent submission on Audacity 4.0's Qt rewrite received the same day. The first, from PR #2354, was reviewed, approved, merged, and published to src/content/articles/2026-09/03-audacity-40-rebuilds-the-open-source-audio-editor-on-qt-with-a-new-clip-editing-model.md before this submission was reviewed. I read the published article in full and compared it line-by-line against this submission: both cover the identical event (Audacity 4.0, released Sept 3 2026) with the identical core facts — Qt rebuild of the wxWidgets interface, new clip-editing/grouping model, Workspaces with saved UI layouts, new .aup4 project format with one-way conversion from .aup3, and the same list of dropped Audacity 3 features (Time Tracks, MIDI tracks, Mixer, Macro Manager/scripting, VAMP/LADSPA, Play-at-speed). Both cite the same GitHub release notes and the same two OMG! Ubuntu articles (June beta + September release) as primary sources, and quote several of the same passages verbatim (e.g. 'built on wxWidgets since the project began, now runs in Qt'; the .aup4 'one way process' conversion language). This submission additionally cites audacityteam.org/audacity-4, audacityteam.org's homepage, and a short LWN.net item, which supply incidental additional color — a download-count stat, accent-color/high-contrast theming detail, and a one-paragraph technical-press blurb — but none of this amounts to a distinct angle, a follow-up development, new information, or a contradicting viewpoint. The published article, by contrast, has an Analysis section noting the Qt 'rewrite' framing is narrower than it sounds (the underlying audio engine is unchanged, bridged via the au3wrap module) plus additional detail (ASIO support, ARM64 builds, Snap/Flathub distribution lag) not present in this submission at all. This submission is a parallel, independently-written account of the same announcement with no meaningful differentiation — it meets the review-submission.md REJECT criterion 'the exact same story was already published ... covers the same news with no new information or angle.'
concerns: Duplicate of the already-published article at src/content/articles/2026-09/03-audacity-40-rebuilds-the-open-source-audio-editor-on-qt-with-a-new-clip-editing-model.md (PR #2354) — same event, same core facts, overlapping primary sources, no new angle or update.

Overview lead states the release 'follow[ed] the Audacity 3.7.9 patch released September 1 and a beta cycle that included a 4.0.0 Beta 4 pre-release on August 28' — this specific is not supported by any of the 6 cited source snapshots.
recommendations: REJECT under v3.9.0 policy: duplicate of already-published coverage with no new information or angle. The work is discarded; no rewrite cycle. If the bot has a genuinely new angle on Audacity 4.0 (e.g. distribution rollout, the au3wrap/engine-unchanged nuance, or a follow-up development), it should research and submit that as a fresh, clearly differentiated submission rather than resubmitting this piece.

Independently of the duplicate issue, the bot should not include specific dates/version numbers (e.g. prior patch or beta release dates) in a lead paragraph unless they are directly supported by a cited source.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: REJECT. This is a same-day duplicate of an already-published article covering the identical Audacity 4.0 Qt-rewrite announcement, with no meaningfully new information or angle — confirmed by direct comparison against the published article and by verifying all 6 source snapshots. A secondary, independent issue (an unsourced patch/beta-history specific in the Overview lead) further supports not publishing as-is.
